When every color is already in the model you chose, or nothing is selected, nothing changes. What is converted Solid fills, the stops of gradients, the colors of mesh fills, patterns and textures. Outlines, text and table cells. The colors of effects (contours, blends, extrusions, bevels, block shadows and the others) and of drop shadows. Objects inside groups and clip frames, at any depth. Bitmaps take the color mode: converted to CMYK, a picture's pixels change to show the colors the inks can print; converted to RGB, only the mode changes and the pixels stay. See Bitmap color modes. The registration color never changes, so marks still print on every plate. Spot colors stay spot colors unless you tick Convert spot colors too. A color that is already in the model stays as it is. How the colors are worked out The conversion goes through the color management profiles: the drawing's own CMYK profile when it carries one, else the RGB and CMYK profiles, the rendering intent and the black point setting of Tools > Color Management. See Color management. Tip: A color converted to CMYK and back to RGB is not the color you started with when it was too bright for the inks. Keep a copy of the drawing before converting a whole drawing.

Spezialeffekte Effekte ändern das Aussehen eines Objekts, ohne das Objekt selbst zu ändern: Eine Überblendung füllt den Raum zwischen zwei Objekten, eine Kontur zeichnet Ringe um eines, eine Hülle verbiegt es, eine Extrusion lässt es massiv wirken, ein Schatten hebt es von der Seite ab. Die meisten Effekte sind dynamisch: Das Objekt behält seine eigene Form, und der Effekt wird daraus gezeichnet, sodass Sie ihn jederzeit ändern oder entfernen können. Die Effekte finden Sie im Menü Effekte, im Flyout Effekte der Hilfsmittelpalette und in eigenen Andockfenstern. Bitmap-Effekte ändern die Pixel von Bildern oder von Objekten, die als Bilder gezeichnet werden.

h: Effekte verwalten Weitere Effektbefehle
x: Das Andockfenster Effekte Ein Objekt kann mehrere Live-Effekte gleichzeitig tragen, die nacheinander angewendet werden. Das Andockfenster Effekte listet die Effekte des ausgewählten Objekts in der Reihenfolge auf, in der sie angewendet werden, von oben nach unten. Öffnen Sie es mit Fenster > Bereiche > Effects.  Effekte verwalten Jede Zeile der Liste hat: ein Kontrollkästchen, das den Effekt ein- oder ausschaltet. Ein ausgeschalteter Effekt behält Platz und Einstellungen, wird aber nicht gezeichnet, exportiert oder gedruckt; den Namen des Effekts, abgeblendet, solange er aus ist; Pfeile nach oben und unten, die den Effekt früher oder später anwenden, was das Ergebnis ändert (zum Beispiel eine Kontur einer Hülle oder eine Hülle einer Kontur); ein Kreuz, das den Effekt entfernt. Jede Änderung ist ein Rückgängig-Schritt. Jeder Effekt wird weiterhin mit seinem eigenen Werkzeug oder Andockfenster bearbeitet. Weitere Effektbefehle Effekte > Effekte reduzieren wandelt die Effekte der ausgewählten Objekte in einfache Objekte um. Effect Picker zeigt eine Liste von Effekten, die auf die Auswahl angewendet werden können. Objekt > Effekt aufheben entfernt den Effekt der Auswahl. Objekt > Effekt kopieren kopiert einen Effekt von einem anderen Objekt, und Effekt klonen erstellt einen Klon, der ihm folgt; siehe Effekte kopieren und klonen.

h: To blend two objects Blend settings Controls on the canvas Blending along a path Removing or splitting a blend Saving as .cdr
x: Blends A blend draws a series of intermediate steps between two objects, changing shape, size and color from one to the other. Use it for smooth shading, repeated patterns or a shape that turns into another. To blend two objects With the tool: Choose the Blend tool from the Effects flyout. Drag from the start object to the end object. With the panel: Select two objects. Open the Blend panel with Effects > Blend (Ctrl+F8). Set the options and click Apply.  Both objects stay objects of the drawing: move, resize or recolor either one and the steps follow. Deleting the end object removes the blend. Blend settings With a blend selected, every change on the property bar or in the panel applies at once. Blend steps: the number of steps (5 at first, up to 999). Spacing, for a blend on a path: the distance between steps; the number of steps follows from the length of the path. Rotation: turns the steps progressively; Loop turns them about the middle between the two objects instead. Acceleration: the object slider makes the steps crowd towards one end; the color slider does the same for the colors. Apply to sizing makes the object acceleration change the sizes too, and Link acceleration keeps the two sliders together. Reset puts both back to even. Color Blend: Direct (straight from one color to the other), Clockwise or Counterclockwise (around the color wheel). The tool's property bar has the steps, rotation and the two accelerations. Controls on the canvas Pick a blend with the Blend tool (click its start or end object, or a step) to show its controls: a square on the start object, a crossed square on the end object, the line between them and two sliders on it, the object acceleration above and the color acceleration below. Drag a slider toward the start or the end to crowd the steps or the colors there. The blend follows live, each drag is one undo step, and the property bar follows. A slider goes as far one way as the other: at 100 % the middle step sits right by the start object, at -100 % right by the end object. Drag an end square to move its object, so the blend changes direction. Drop it on another object to make that object the new start or end, with the blend's settings. The object acceleration moves the steps toward one end also when the blend follows no path. A bitmap effect on the start object keeps the blend drawn. Blending along a path Select the blend. Click New path in the Blend panel and click a curve. The steps follow the curve. Rotate all objects turns each step along the curve, and Blend along full path places the first and last steps at the ends of the curve. Removing or splitting a blend Clear blend removes the steps and leaves both objects. Break apart turns the steps into objects of their own, grouped. Object > Break Blend Group Apart (Ctrl+K, also on the right-click menu) does the same. Saving as .cdr A blend saved as .cdr (version 9 or later) stays a blend: the file holds the two objects and the blend record between them, so the program that opens the file shows the steps and lets you change the blend. The steps, spacing and the two objects go into the file; acceleration, rotation, a path and the colour direction come back in TraceDraw (version 14 or later), other programs start from their defaults.

h: Eine Kontur hinzufügen Kontureinstellungen
x: Konturen Eine Kontur zeichnet gleichmäßig beabstandete Kopien des Umrisses eines Objekts nach innen, nach außen oder bis zu seiner Mitte, wie die Linien einer Karte. Sie ist ein Live-Effekt: Ändern Sie das Objekt, folgt die Kontur. Eine Kontur hinzufügen Mit dem Werkzeug: Wählen Sie das Werkzeug Kontur aus dem Flyout für Effekte. Ziehen Sie von einem Objekt aus: von seiner Mitte weg für eine äußere Kontur, zu ihr hin für eine innere. Je weiter Sie ziehen, desto größer der Abstand. Mit dem Andockfenster: Wählen Sie ein Objekt aus. Öffnen Sie das Andockfenster Kontur mit Effekte > Kontur (Ctrl+F9). Stellen Sie die Optionen ein und klicken Sie auf Zuweisen.  Gruppen und Bitmaps können keine Kontur erhalten. Kontureinstellungen Die Eigenschaftsleiste und das Andockfenster zeigen die Einstellungen der ausgewählten Kontur und ändern sie sofort. Zur Mitte, Innen oder Außen (anfangs). Schritte: anfangs 3, bis zu 999. Zur Mitte erstellt so viele, wie hineinpassen. Versatz: der Abstand zwischen den Schritten (anfangs 2 mm). Ecken: spitz (anfangs), rund oder abgeschrägt. Farbrichtung: direkt, im Uhrzeigersinn oder gegen den Uhrzeigersinn um den Farbkreis, von den Farben des Objekts zu denen des letzten Schritts. Die Füll- und Umrissfarben des letzten Schritts (anfangs Weiß und Schwarz). Ein Objekt ohne Füllung ergibt ungefüllte Schritte. Objektbeschleunigung und Farbbeschleunigung (-100 bis 100 %) drängen die Schritte oder die Farben zum Objekt oder zum letzten Schritt hin. Äußere Schritte werden hinter dem Objekt gezeichnet, innere davor. Kontur entfernen entfernt die Kontur; Kombination aufheben wandelt die Schritte in Objekte um. Die Schritte werden neben dem Objekt gruppiert. Objekt > Break Contour Group Apart (Strg+K, auch im Kontextmenü) bewirkt dasselbe.

h: Ein Objekt verzerren Verzerrungseinstellungen
x: Verzerrung Das Werkzeug Verzerren verbiegt den Umriss eines Objekts auf drei Arten: Drücken und Ziehen (Zacken oder Blütenblätter), Zickzack (Zickzackzähne) und Verdrehen (ein Wirbel). Es ist ein Live-Effekt: Sie können die Verzerrung jederzeit ändern, verschieben oder entfernen, und das Objekt behält seinen eigenen Umriss. Ein Objekt verzerren Wählen Sie das Werkzeug Verzerren aus dem Flyout für Effekte. Wählen Sie die Art in der Eigenschaftsleiste. Ziehen Sie auf dem Objekt. Die Verzerrung wird dort zentriert, wo Sie beginnen. Drücken und Ziehen: Ziehen Sie nach rechts, um die Knoten nach außen zu drücken (zackige Formen mit hohlen Seiten), nach links, um sie nach innen zu ziehen (runde Blütenblätter). Zickzack: Je weiter Sie ziehen, desto höher die Zähne. Verdrehen: Ziehen Sie um den Startpunkt herum; volle Umdrehungen zählen. Der Mittelpunkt einer ausgewählten Verzerrung wird als Raute angezeigt: Ziehen Sie sie, um den Mittelpunkt zu verschieben. Erneutes Ziehen ersetzt die Verzerrung; ein Objekt hat höchstens eine. Gruppen und Bitmaps werden nicht verzerrt. Verzerrungseinstellungen Die Eigenschaftsleiste zeigt und ändert die ausgewählte Verzerrung: die Art: Drücken und Ziehen, Zickzack oder Verdrehen (die Wahl einer anderen Art ändert eine ausgewählte Verzerrung); bei Drücken und Ziehen die Amplitude (-200 bis 200, anfangs 20); bei Zickzack die Amplitude (0 bis 100 mm, anfangs 2 mm) und die Frequenz (Zähne pro Segment, anfangs 6), mit Zufällig (ungleichmäßige Zähne), Glatt (abgerundete Zähne) und Lokal (Zähne werden vom Mittelpunkt weg kleiner); bei Verdrehen im Uhrzeigersinn oder gegen den Uhrzeigersinn, die Anzahl ganzer Umdrehungen und die zusätzlichen Grad. Objekt > Effekt aufheben entfernt die Verzerrung.

h: To add an envelope Editing the frame Envelope settings
x: Envelopes An envelope is a frame of nodes around an object; the object is bent to fill the frame, and follows when you move its nodes. Use it to arch text, bulge a shape or fit artwork into a flag or a circle. The object keeps its own shape, so the envelope can be changed or removed at any time. To add an envelope With the tool: Choose the Envelope tool from the Effects flyout. Click an object. It gets a frame of eight nodes: the corners and the middle of each side. Drag the nodes to reshape the frame. With the panel (Effects > Envelope, Ctrl+F7): Select an object. Click Add new, or click one of the 24 preset shapes (arch, circle, flag, heart, cloud, speech bubble and more) to use it as the envelope.  Editing the frame The editing mode, chosen on the property bar or in the panel, decides what happens to the sides when you drag a node: Straight line: the sides stay straight; Single arc: the sides become one smooth arc; Double arc: the sides become S curves; Unconstrained (at first): the node carries its handles; click a node to see its two handles and drag them to bend each side on its own. Double-click the frame to add a node, a node (other than a corner) to delete it. In the unconstrained mode the property bar also has Add node and Delete node. The Shape tool edits the frame the same way. Envelope settings Presets on the property bar: arch, bulge, squeeze, flag, perspective and circle. Mapping, how the object fills the frame: Putty (at first), Original (spread evenly along the frame), Horizontal or Vertical (only across or only up). Keep lines: straight segments of the object stay straight. Add new envelope puts a fresh frame around the object as it now looks, over the envelope it has. Copy envelope properties: click another object to copy its envelope (as Object > Copy Effect > Envelope From). Click an object without an envelope, such as a circle, a star or a curve you drew, to fit the selected text or objects into its shape. Clear envelope removes the last envelope.

h: Place the photo and the design Follow the chest with an envelope Let the cloth show through: Multiply Keep the print on the shirt: a clip frame Tips
x: Making a T-shirt mockup A mockup shows a design on a photo of the real thing, here a T-shirt, so you can judge it before it is printed. Four tools from the rest of this Help do the work: an envelope bends the design over the chest, a transparency merge mode lets the cloth's folds and shading show through the print, and a clip frame keeps the print on the shirt.  Place the photo and the design Choose File > Import and import a photo of a plain shirt, front view, in good light. Draw or import your design, place it over the chest and size it there. If the design is made of several objects, select them all and choose Object > Group, so the next steps treat it as one. Follow the chest with an envelope Cloth is not flat. A slight curve makes the print look as if it lies on the shirt. Select the design and choose the Envelope tool (or open Effects > Envelope). Use Single arc and drag the middle nodes a little: the bottom one down, the top one up and the side ones out. Keep it subtle. Each object of a group is bent from the box of the whole group and keeps its own colours. See Envelopes.  Let the cloth show through: Multiply A print takes on the shading of the cloth under it. The Multiply merge mode does the same: each color is multiplied by what is beneath, so the folds and shadows of the photo darken the design where they darken the shirt. Select the design and choose the Transparency tool, or open the transparency settings in the Properties panel. Choose Uniform and set the amount low (0 to 10 %). Set Merge mode to Multiply. See Transparency.  Keep the print on the shirt: a clip frame A large print, or one placed near a sleeve, can reach past the shirt's edges.  Draw the outline of the shirt over the photo with the Bezier or Pen tool, following its edges (it does not need to be exact where the print does not reach). Give it no fill and no outline. Select the design, choose Object > Clip to Frame > Place Inside Frame and click the outline. The print is cut to the shirt and keeps its Multiply merge mode: it still mixes with the photo beneath the frame. See Placing objects inside a frame.  Tips A white or light shirt shows Multiply best. On a dark shirt, try If Lighter for a light print, or keep Normal with a little transparency. To try another design, use Edit Contents, or Extract Contents, replace the design and place the new one inside again. Group the photo, the frame and the design to move the whole mockup.

h: To extrude an object Extrusion settings
x: Extrusions An extrusion turns a flat object into a solid-looking body, with sides that run from its outline to a copy of it, lit and shaded. It is a live effect: change the object and the body follows. To extrude an object With the tool: Choose the Extrude tool from the Effects flyout. Drag from an object. For a parallel extrusion the body runs along the drag; for the others the end of the drag is the vanishing point. Drag the handle (a square with a cross) to move the vanishing point. With the panel (Effects > Extrude, Ctrl+F10): select an object, set the options and click Apply.  Groups and bitmaps cannot be extruded. Extrusion settings The panel has five pages, chosen with the buttons at its top; the property bar has the main settings and a 3D menu with the rest. Camera: the type of extrusion: small back (at first), big back, small front, big front, back parallel or front parallel. Back types grow behind the object, front types in front of it. The depth (1 to 99, 20 at first), the vanishing point (X and Y, counted from the page origin or the object's center), and whether it is locked to the object (moves with it) or to the page. For parallel types, X and Y are the offset. Rotation: turns the body in space about X, Y and Z (-360 to 360 degrees); Reset puts it back. Lighting: the angle (135 degrees at first), intensity (50 at first) and elevation of the light, and two more lights you can turn on. Color: Object fill (the object's color, at first), Solid (one color) or Shade (a gradient from one color to another on each side). Bevel: a beveled edge on the front face, with its width. Clear extrude removes the extrusion; Break apart turns the faces into objects, grouped beside the object. Object > Break Extrude Group Apart (Ctrl+K, also on the right-click menu) does the same.

h: Einen Blockschatten hinzufügen Einstellungen
x: Blockschatten Ein Blockschatten ist ein massiver Schatten, der geradlinig von einem Objekt ausgeht, als wäre das Objekt ein dicker Block. Er wird unter dem Objekt als eine gefüllte Form gezeichnet, was sich für Schilder und Folienschnitt eignet. Einen Blockschatten hinzufügen Wählen Sie das Werkzeug Blockschatten aus dem Flyout für Effekte. Ziehen Sie von einem Objekt in die Richtung, in die der Schatten gehen soll. Einstellungen In der Eigenschaftsleiste: Tiefe: wie weit der Schatten reicht. Richtung: sein Winkel, 0 nach rechts, gegen den Uhrzeigersinn. Farbe: anfangs 60 % Schwarz. Abstand: ein freier Streifen zwischen Objekt und Schatten (anfangs 0). Blockschatten entfernen entfernt den Effekt. Ist ein Objekt mit Schatten ausgewählt, ändern die Felder seinen Schatten; andernfalls legen sie den nächsten fest.

h: Einen hinterlegten Schatten hinzufügen Einstellungen
x: Hinterlegte Schatten Maschinelle Übersetzung: Diese Seite kann hinter der englischen Fassung zurückliegen. Ein hinterlegter Schatten ist ein weicher Schatten unter einem Objekt, als ob es über der Seite schweben würde. Er ist eine Kopie der Silhouette des Objekts in der Schattenfarbe, versetzt und weichgezeichnet. Einen hinterlegten Schatten hinzufügen Wählen Sie das Werkzeug Hinterlegter Schatten aus dem Flyout für Effekte. Ziehen Sie von einem Objekt dorthin, wo der Schatten fallen soll. Auch Clip-Rahmen und Gruppen erhalten Schatten: Ein Rahmen wirft den Schatten dessen, was er zeigt (seine Füllung und den Inhalt darin), eine Gruppe den Schatten jedes ihrer Objekte. Ein Klick auf einen Schatten mit dem Werkzeug Auswahl wählt sein Objekt aus; mit dem Werkzeug Hinterlegter Schatten zeigt er die Griffe des Schattens, und Ziehen am Schatten verschiebt ihn. Schatten erscheinen in exportierten und gedruckten PDF-Dateien, mit Farbe, Deckkraft und weicher Kante. Einstellungen In der Eigenschaftsleiste: der Versatz des Schattens (anfangs 2 mm nach rechts und 2 mm nach unten); seine Deckkraft (anfangs 50 %); seine Randauflösung, also wie weich seine Kante ist (anfangs 15 %); seine Farbe (anfangs Schwarz). Objekt > Effekt aufheben entfernt den Schatten. Um den Schatten eines anderen Objekts zu kopieren, verwenden Sie Objekt > Effekt kopieren > Hinterlegter Schatten von.

h: Ein Objekt abschrägen
x: Abschrägungen Eine Abschrägung lässt die Kanten eines Objekts erhaben oder eingraviert wirken, indem sie eine Seite der Kante beleuchtet und die andere schattiert. Sie ist ein Live-Effekt, der im Andockfenster Abschrägung eingestellt wird; öffnen Sie es mit Effekte > Abschrägung.  Ein Objekt abschrägen Wählen Sie ein gefülltes Objekt aus. Wählen Sie im Andockfenster Abschrägung den Stil: Weiche Kante: Die Kante fällt zum Objekt hin ab, auf einer Seite beleuchtet und auf der anderen schattiert; Relief: Das Objekt scheint aus der Seite herausgeprägt. Stellen Sie das Aussehen der Abschrägung ein: Tiefe: wie weit die Abschrägung von der Kante reicht, beim weichen Rand ins Objekt hinein, beim Relief nach außen; Stufe: in wie viele Stufen Licht und Schatten über die Abschrägung verteilt werden. 1 ergibt zwei flache Töne, mehr Stufen verlaufen weich von der Kante nach innen; Lichtwinkel: die Richtung, aus der das Licht kommt; Intensität: wie stark Licht und Schatten sind; Lichtfarbe und Schattenfarbe: die Farben der beleuchteten und der schattierten Seite; Reliefarbe: die Farbe, aus der die Abschrägung abgetönt wird. Setzen Sie das Häkchen und wählen Sie eine eigene Farbe; ausgeschaltet gilt die Füllung des Objekts. Klicken Sie auf Zuweisen. Um eine Abschrägung von einem anderen Objekt zu kopieren, verwenden Sie Objekt > Effekt kopieren > Abschrägung von. Objekt > Effekt aufheben entfernt sie. Das Andockfenster für Extrusionen hat ebenfalls eine Abschrägung für die Vorderseite; siehe Extrusionen.

h: To make a lens Kinds of lens Options
x: Lenses A lens changes how the objects beneath it look, without changing them: it can brighten, tint, magnify, invert or apply bitmap effects to everything it covers. Move the lens and the view through it changes. Lenses are set in the Lens panel (Effects > Lens, Alt+F3).  To make a lens Draw a closed object over the objects to change, and select it. In the Lens panel, choose the kind of lens and its settings. Click Apply. Kinds of lens Brighten brightens (or darkens) what lies beneath rate, -100 to 100 (50) Color add adds a color, as light color and rate Color limit lets only a color through color and rate Custom color map maps dark to light onto a range of colors from and to colors, direction Fish eye bulges what lies beneath rate, -1000 to 1000 (100) Heat map shows brightness as warm and cold colors palette rotation Invert inverts the colors  Magnify enlarges what lies beneath amount, 1 to 100 (2) Tinted grayscale shows it in shades of one color color Transparency makes the lens see-through, tinted rate and color Wireframe shows the objects as outlines outline and fill colors Bitmap effects runs bitmap effects over what lies beneath Add effect, in order Options Frozen: keeps what the lens shows now, even when the objects beneath change. Viewpoint: shows another place through the lens. Remove face: shows the lens only over other objects, not over the empty page. To add a bitmap effect as a lens from the effect picker, choose Effects > Effect Picker and apply it as a lens.

h: Einem Objekt Perspektive geben Perspektivisch zeichnen
x: Perspektive Perspektive lässt ein Objekt so aussehen, als läge es auf einer Ebene, die in die Ferne zurückweicht. Sie können einem gezeichneten Objekt Perspektive geben oder direkt auf einem Perspektivraster zeichnen. Einem Objekt Perspektive geben Wählen Sie ein Objekt aus. Wählen Sie Objekt > Perspektive hinzufügen. Ziehen Sie die vier Eckknoten mit dem Werkzeug Form, um es zu kippen. Um die Perspektive eines anderen Objekts zu kopieren, verwenden Sie Objekt > Effekt kopieren > Perspektive von. Perspektivisch zeichnen Ansicht > Draw in Perspective zeigt ein Perspektivraster über der Seite. Solange es aktiv ist, wird jedes Objekt, das ein Zeichenwerkzeug erstellt (Rechtecke, Ellipsen, Polygone, Kurven, Pinselstriche, Textrahmen), auf die aktive Ebene des Rasters gelegt. Objekte, die Sie einfügen, duplizieren oder mit dem Werkzeug Auswahl verschieben, bleiben, wie sie sind. Die Leiste oben links im Zeichenfenster enthält: Fertig stellen: verlässt den Modus; die Objekte behalten ihre Perspektive; 1-Punkt, 2-Punkt und 3-Punkt: die Art des Rasters; die Ebenen: Boden, Links, Rechts (und Oben bei einem 1-Punkt-Raster). Die aktive Ebene wird kräftig gezeichnet; Raster: zeigt die Rasterlinien; Tiefe (5 bis 98 %): wie weit das Raster in Richtung der Fluchtpunkte reicht; Auf Ebene legen: legt die ausgewählten Objekte auf die aktive Ebene. Ziehen Sie die Fluchtpunkte (Kreise) und die vorderen Ecken (Quadrate), um das Raster zu ändern. Ein auf eine Ebene gelegtes Objekt erhält einen gewöhnlichen Perspektiveffekt, dessen vier Ecken Sie weiterhin mit dem Werkzeug Form bearbeiten können.

h: Einen Effekt kopieren Einen Effekt klonen
x: Effekte kopieren und klonen Statt einen Effekt erneut einzurichten, können Sie ihn von einem Objekt kopieren, das ihn bereits hat. Einen Effekt kopieren Wählen Sie die Objekte aus, die den Effekt erhalten sollen. Wählen Sie Objekt > Effekt kopieren und die Art des Effekts: Hinterlegter Schatten von, Transparenz von, Hülle von, Perspektive von, Verzerrung von, Extrusion von, Kontur von, Überblendung von, Linse von, Abschrägung von oder Blockschatten von. Klicken Sie auf das Objekt, von dem kopiert werden soll. Ein Rechtsklick bricht ab. Der Effekt wird an jedes Objekt angepasst: Eine Hülle oder Perspektive wird auf seine Größe gestreckt, eine Verzerrung behält ihren Mittelpunkt an derselben Stelle innerhalb des Objekts. Hat das angeklickte Objekt keinen solchen Effekt, ändert sich nichts, und die Statusleiste weist darauf hin. Das Kopieren ist ein einziger Rückgängig-Schritt. Einen Effekt klonen Objekt > Effekt klonen kopiert den Schatten (Schatten von) oder die Transparenz (Transparenz von) eines anderen Objekts und folgt ihm weiterhin: Ändern Sie die Quelle, ändern sich auch die Klone, bis Sie den eigenen Effekt eines Klons bearbeiten. Bearbeiten > Klonen erstellt einen Klon eines ganzen Objekts, und Eigenschaften kopieren von kopiert die Füllung, den Umriss oder die Texteigenschaften eines anderen Objekts.

h: Vector Mosaic Picture Mosaic
x: Vector and picture mosaics A mosaic rebuilds the selected objects, or a picture, out of many small tiles. A vector mosaic uses colored shapes; a picture mosaic uses photos from a folder of your own. Vector Mosaic Open the Vector Mosaic panel with Effects > Vector Mosaic.  Select the objects or bitmaps to turn into a mosaic. Set the options: Density: tiles per inch (10 at first); Scale: the size of each tile within its cell (1 at first); Screen angle: how the rows are turned (30 degrees at first). Keep original: off deletes the selection once the mosaic is made. Limit colors: reduce the tiles to at most that many colors (16 at first). Method: Uniform (every tile full size, transparency flattened on white), Size modulation 1 (the tile size follows the opacity, at first) or Size modulation 2 (darker areas give bigger tiles). Merge adjacent: combine up to that many neighbouring tiles of one color; Weld adjacent overlap: one curve per color instead of one object per tile. Shape: circle (at first), square or custom. For a custom tile, select a closed curve and click Select. Click Apply. The mosaic is one group placed on top of the selection, and is selected. Picture Mosaic Open the Picture Mosaic panel with Effects > Picture Mosaic.  Select the objects or bitmaps to rebuild. Under Library, click Browse and choose a folder of pictures (PNG, JPEG, BMP, GIF, WebP or TIFF; up to 1000). The panel shows how many it holds. Set the options: Keep original (on at first). Columns: tiles across (30 at first); the rows follow from the shape of the selection. Blending: how much of the selection shows over the tiles (20% at first). Allow duplicates (on), with the tile spacing: the fewest tiles between two uses of one picture. Composition: single, stack or array; Edges: stretch the last row or remove it; Output priority and the resolution: how large the mosaic is in pixels. The panel shows the resulting size. Click Apply. Note: Picture libraries need the desktop version; the browser version cannot read folders.

h: To apply a bitmap effect The effect groups Special dialogs Editing the effects of an object The Effect Picker Effects that spread past the edges
x: Bitmap effects Bitmap effects change pixels: blur, sharpen, adjust colors, add textures and artistic strokes. They work on bitmaps and also on vector objects, which are then drawn as the picture the effects make while keeping their own shape, fill and outline. Effects are kept apart from the original pixels: you can edit, hide, reorder or remove any of them later, and removing the last one gives the original back. To apply a bitmap effect Select one or more objects. Choose a group in the Effects menu and an effect. Effects without settings apply at once. The others open a dialog box you can size, with the first selected object before and after in the Before and After preview and the settings on the right. The effect also shows on the drawing and follows every value as it changes (untick Preview to switch that off); the work is done in the background, so the window keeps answering on large pictures. Click OK to keep what the drawing shows as one undo step; Cancel or Esc put the drawing back exactly as it was. Reset puts every setting back to its default.  The change to the whole selection is one undo step. With a bitmap selected, Ctrl+B opens Brightness/Contrast/Intensity, Ctrl+Shift+B Color Balance and Ctrl+Shift+U Hue/Saturation/Lightness. The effect groups 3D Effects Cylinder, Emboss, Page Curl, Pinch/Punch, Sphere Adjust Auto Adjust, Image Adjustments, Contrast Enhancement, Local Equalization, Target Color Balance, Tone Curve, Brightness/Contrast/Intensity, Color Balance, Gamma, Hue/Saturation/Lightness, Selective Color, Replace Colors, Desaturate, Channel Mixer Art Strokes Charcoal, Conté Crayon, Crayon, Cubist, Impressionist, Palette Knife, Pastels, Pen & Ink, Pointillist, Scraperboard, Sketch Pad, Watercolor, Felt Marker, Paper Grain Blur Directional Smooth, Gaussian Blur, Smooth Jagged Edges, Low Pass, Motion Blur, Radial Blur, Smart Blur, Smooth, Soften, Zoom Camera Colorize, Diffuse, Photo Filter, Sepia Toning, Vintage Photo Color Transform Bit Planes, Halftone, Psychedelic, Solarize Contour Edge Detect, Find Edges, Trace Contour Correction Dust and Scratch Creative Crystallize, Fabric, Frame, Glass Tiles, Mosaic, Scatter, Tinted Glass, Stained Glass, Vignette, Vortex Custom Bump Map Distort Blocks, Displace, Mesh Warp, Offset, Pixelate, Ripple, Swirl, Tile, Wet Paint, Whirlpool, Wind Noise Add Noise, Maximum, Median, Minimum, Remove Moiré, Remove Noise Sharpen Adaptive Unsharp, Directional Sharpen, High Pass, Sharpen, Unsharp Mask Texture Cobblestone, Wrinkles, Etching, Plastic, Relief Sculpture, Stone Transform Deinterlace, Invert Colors, Posterize Special dialogs Image Adjustments opens a larger dialog box: a large preview you can zoom, pan and rotate, shown alone, side by side or split; Auto adjust and pickers for the white and black points; sliders for temperature, tint, saturation, brightness, contrast, highlights, shadows and midtones, with a histogram; undo and redo inside the dialog; and snapshots of settings to compare. Contrast Enhancement shows the histogram with markers to drag for the input and output levels, eyedroppers for black and white, and Auto adjust. Tone Curve edits a curve per channel (master, red, green, blue) in four styles (curve, straight, freehand, gamma), over the histogram; curves can be saved and loaded. Colors of the picture, such as in Replace Colors, have an eyedropper: click a preview to take the color under the pointer. Editing the effects of an object The FX section of the Properties panel lists the effects of the selected object, first applied at the top. Each row has a check box to show or hide the effect, Edit (opens its dialog box), Move up, Move down and Delete. Add effect opens the effect groups. Effects > Flatten Effects makes the effects permanent: a bitmap keeps what it shows, and a vector object becomes a bitmap. The Effect Picker Effects > Effect Picker opens a window that stays open while you work, with every effect as a small picture. Type in the search field to find effects, or choose a group or Recent from the list. With something selected, click a tile to apply the effect. You can also apply an effect as a lens. Effects that spread past the edges Blurs and similar effects can reach past the edges of a bitmap. With Bitmaps > Inflate Bitmap > Auto Inflate Bitmap on (as at first), the bitmap grows to make room for them. See Resampling and straightening. To save a bitmap with its effects as a PNG file, right-click it and choose Save Bitmap As.

Text TraceDraw kennt zwei Arten von Text. Grafiktext ist eine Zeile oder einige Zeilen an einem Punkt: Titel, Beschriftungen, Logos. Mengentext fließt in einem Rahmen und bricht an dessen Rändern um: Fließtext, Spalten, Listen. Beide lassen sich Zeichen für Zeichen formatieren, an Pfade anpassen und auf Rechtschreibung prüfen. Diese Seiten erklären, wie Sie Text hinzufügen und formatieren, Absätze gestalten, Schriften und Sonderzeichen wählen und die Schreibwerkzeuge nutzen.

h: Adding text Editing text Formatting from the property bar The Text panel Paragraph text frames Moving and turning characters Text on a path Other text commands
x: Adding and editing text Adding text Choose the Text tool (F8). For artistic text, click where the text starts and type. Press Enter to start a new line. For paragraph text, drag a frame, then type. The text wraps at the edges of the frame. Press Esc to finish. An empty text is removed. New artistic text is 24 points, paragraph text 12 points, in the first sans-serif font found. Change the defaults by formatting with nothing selected. To make an existing object a text frame, right-click it and choose to create an empty text frame; see Empty frames. Text > Insert Placeholder Text fills the selected frames with sample text, as much as fits. Editing text Click text with the Text tool, or double-click it with the Pick tool, to edit it in place. Text > Edit Text (Ctrl+Shift+T) opens a box with the whole text to edit instead; OK puts it back in the drawing, and the characters you did not change keep their formatting. Typing, Ctrl+V insert at the caret, replacing the selection Backspace, Delete delete the selection, else the character before or after Enter, Shift+Enter new paragraph, new line Arrow keys, with Ctrl move by a character or a word; Shift selects Home, End, with Ctrl start or end of the line, or of the text Ctrl+A select all Ctrl+B, Ctrl+I, Ctrl+U bold, italic, underline Ctrl+L, Ctrl+E, Ctrl+R align left, center, right Ctrl+J, Ctrl+H, Ctrl+N full justify, force justify, no alignment Shift+F3 change case (see Writing tools) Double-click select a word A new alignment keeps artistic text in place at the reference point of the X and Y fields of the property bar; in a frame it applies to the paragraphs at the caret. Text in right-to-left scripts (Arabic, Hebrew) is laid out right to left, also when it is mixed with left-to-right words, and selections shade every selected letter. Keyboards and input methods that send characters (such as those for Tamil and other Indian scripts on Windows) type into text and fields, and Alt codes typed on the keypad give their character once. All your typing in one editing session is one undo step. Formatting from the property bar With the Text tool, or with text selected, the property bar has the font list, the size (type it or pick from the list), bold, italic, underline, the alignment (left, center, right, full justify), bullets and drop cap for paragraph text, Text (Ctrl+T) and Edit Text. The button beside the font size opens the sliders of a variable font's axes (see Variable fonts). While editing, they act on the selected characters; otherwise on the whole selected texts. Your choice also becomes the default for the next text. The font list shows each family in its own font, with the ones you used last at the top. Type to narrow the list. A family with several styles has an arrow that shows them. See Fonts and glyphs. The Text panel The Text panel (Ctrl+T) has every text setting, in three sections you can open and close: Character, Paragraph and Frame. The three buttons at the top show the panel from that section on. Full justification spreads Chinese and Japanese lines to the edge of the frame by adding room between the characters, and paragraph text in those scripts breaks lines by their rules: punctuation such as ，。、 and closing brackets never start a line, and opening brackets never end one. Letters given another color keep the font's kerning with their neighbours.  Character: the font, style and size; range kerning (-50 to 200%) and underline; the fill, background and outline of the characters. More options under the section: character offsets and angle, strikethrough and OpenType features. Paragraph: the alignment (none, left, center, right, full justify, and forced justify, which spreads the last line too); line spacing in percent of the character height, points or percent of the font size; left, first-line and right indents; space before and after paragraphs; character and word spacing. The gear opens custom hyphens. Frame, for paragraph text: the background color of the frame, the vertical alignment (top, middle, bottom), fit text to frame, columns (1 to 8) and the gap between them, and links to the bullets, drop cap and columns dialog boxes, and hyphenation. Every change applies to the selected characters while editing, or to the selected texts, and is one undo step. With no text selected, the settings become those of new text. The button at the top right gives new text the settings of the selected text. Paragraph text frames Frames show as dashed lines. A frame turns red, with a small tab under its bottom edge, when its text does not fit; the text that does not fit is not drawn, printed or exported. To make it fit: drag the frame's handles to enlarge it. The text flows again; the letters keep their size; choose Text > Paragraph Text Frame > Fit Text to Frame to resize the text to fill the frame; link the frame to another one, so the text flows on: Link. Unlink breaks the link. Or click the small tab under the frame's bottom edge, then click another frame (on this page or another one) or click or drag on an empty spot for a new frame: the text flows on into it. Text > Show Text Frames shows or hides the frames. Moving and turning characters With the Shape tool, text shows a node at each character: drag nodes to move characters, and drag the arrows at the corners of the text to change the character, word and line spacing. The character offsets and angle can also be typed in the Text panel. Text > Straighten Text puts characters back in line, and Align to Baseline (Alt+F12) removes their vertical offsets. Text on a path Select a text and a curve or shape. Choose Text > Fit Text to Path. Or click the outline of a path with the Text tool and type. Text on a closed shape stands on its outside, centered on its top; clicked on the bottom of an ellipse, it starts there. With text on a path selected (also with the Pick tool), the property bar shows the path's fields first, then the usual text fields: The orientation of the letters: rotated, vertical

t: Tabs, columns, bullets and drop caps
h: Tabs Columns Bullets Drop caps Hyphenation
x: Tabs, columns, bullets and drop caps The Text menu has four dialog boxes for laying out paragraph text. Each acts on the selected paragraph text. Their settings are also in the Frame section of the Text panel. Tabs Text > Tabs sets where the Tab character jumps to. At first there is a tab stop every 12.7 mm (half an inch). Select the paragraph text. Choose Text > Tabs. Under Tab stops, change the positions, or click Add tab to add one. Click Close.  Columns Text > Columns splits a text frame into columns; the text flows from one column into the next. Select the paragraph text. Choose Text > Columns. Set the number of Columns and the Gutter, the space between columns (5 mm at first). Click Close.  To break to the next column at a given place, insert Column/Frame Break from Insert Formatting Code. Bullets Text > Bullets puts a bullet before each paragraph. Select the paragraph text. Choose Text > Bullets. Tick Use bullets, and set the bullet Symbol and the Indent (5 mm at first). Click Close.  Drop caps A drop cap is a large first letter that spans several lines. Select the paragraph text. Choose Text > Drop Cap. Tick Use drop cap and set the Lines dropped (3 at first). Click Close. The letter is scaled so its top meets the top of the first line and it sits on the baseline of the last line it spans; the lines beside it are shortened to make room.  Hyphenation Text > Use Hyphenation lets the selected text's words break at the end of lines (while you type in a text, the paragraphs at the cursor; with no text selected, it is the setting for new text), with at least two letters before and three after the break. A comma or other punctuation next to a word does not stop it from breaking, and words with an apostrophe (such as Italian dell'anno) break too. Words with a capital letter are never broken. To decide yourself where a word may break, see Custom hyphens.

h: The Fonts panel Font lists and the filter Variable fonts Missing fonts The Font Sampler The Glyphs panel The Font Manager
x: Fonts and glyphs TraceDraw uses the fonts installed on your computer, fonts you add in the Font Manager, and fonts that come with a drawing. This page explains the panels and the dialog box for working with fonts and special characters. The Fonts panel The Fonts panel lists the font families.  Type in the filter field to narrow the list. Under Fonts in document are the families the drawing uses. A family that is not installed is marked missing; its text shows in a similar font and keeps its font name. A family that came with the drawing is marked embedded. Click a family to give it to the selected text, or to make it the font of new text. Font lists and the filter The font lists of the property bar, the Text panel, the Glyphs panel and the options work the same way: Type to jump to a family. The last five families you picked are at the top ("used last"), and every family's name is drawn in its own font. The mouse wheel over the closed list picks the next or previous family for the text being edited or selected. A font that came with the drawing and is not installed says "Embedded" at the end of its row and after its name in the font box: its text is drawn with the copy that came with the drawing. The Filter button at the top of the open list shows the filter's choices beside the list. Each click filters at once and leaves the list open; the button counts the choices made, such as "Filter (2)", and Clear filter at the top of the choices removes them. The choices, in sections that fold: Fonts shown: all fonts, installed fonts, the fonts in this drawing, or in the browser version the fonts to download. Style: serif, sans serif, script, decorative, monospaced, symbol. Weight: light, regular, bold. Width: condensed, normal, expanded. Technology: TrueType, OpenType, variable. Scripts: Latin, Greek, Cyrillic, Hebrew, Arabic, Devanagari, Bengali, Thai, Korean, Japanese, Chinese and symbols. OpenType features: ligatures, kerning, small capitals, the kinds of figures, fractions, superscripts and subscripts, ordinals, slashed zero, swashes, alternates and stylistic sets, each on its own. Embedding rights: installable, editable, preview and print, restricted, bitmap only. Folders: the folders the installed fonts are in. Within a section a family needs one of the ticked choices (every ticked one for the OpenType features), and it needs what every section asks. The values are read from the font files themselves; with thousands of fonts the list fills in over a moment the first time. Variable fonts A variable font holds a range of weights, widths and other designs in one file. To set them on text: Select the text, or the letters, in a variable font. Click the button beside the font size on the property bar (or in the first section of the Text panel). It is greyed out, with a tip saying why, when the font is not variable. The Character section of the Text panel shows the same sliders. Drag the slider of an axis: Weight, Width, Slant, Italic, Optical size, or the font's own axes by the names it gives them, each over the font's range. The text follows the slider while you drag, so you can judge it on the page. Letting go of the slider, or typing a value, keeps it as one undo step. Default axes takes the values off. The values are saved in .tdraw files and drawn in exports and PDF files; a weight set this way replaces the bold TraceDraw would otherwise draw. Missing fonts When a drawing uses fonts that are not installed, the Missing Fonts dialog box asks which installed font draws each one, for this session or for good. See Missing fonts. Install the fonts and the text shows in them again. Drawings saved as .tdraw, and .cdr files with embedded fonts, can carry their fonts along. The Font Sampler The Font Sampler panel (Text > Font Sampler) shows a line of sample text in several fonts, one under the other, to compare them.  Type the sample text at the top; left empty, a sentence in your interface language is used. Set the size (10 to 96, 28 at first). Add fonts by typing part of a name and clicking one of the matches (up to 24 fonts); the cross removes one. At first the panel lists the text font and the fonts of the drawing. Click a sample to give that font to the selected text. The Glyphs panel The Glyphs panel (Text > Glyphs, Ctrl+F11) shows every character of a font, to insert symbols and special characters.  Choose the font. Choose a character range: the entire font, Basic Latin, Latin-1 Supplement, Latin Extended, Greek, Cyrillic, Hebrew, Arabic, punctuation, numbers, currency, arrows, mathematical operators or symbols. Click a character. It is inserted at the caret of the text you are editing, or as a new text in the middle of the page. Hover a character to see its name and code. A small arrow under a character means the font has alternates for it (such as swashes or small capitals); click it to see them. The glyphs you used last are at the top of the panel. Type in the search field above the grid to find characters: type the characters themselves (such as é), or a Unicode code point such as U+20AC, 0x20ac or 20AC. The line above the grid shows the code point, the character and the range of the character under the pointer. The Font Manager Tools > Font Manager opens the Font Manager, a window that organizes your fonts.  Libraries (top left): My fonts (the installed fonts), the folders you added, Favorites and your collections. Double-click a collection to rename it; right-click for more. Filters (bottom left): by status (installed, not installed, protected system fonts, duplicates), embedding rights, technology (TrueType, OpenType, variable), weight, width, style, character range and OpenType features. Clear removes them. Right side: the sample text and its presets, a search field (family, style or PostScript name), and the fonts as cards, grouped by family. Each card shows a sample, the technology and a bar that is green when the font is installed. Click to pick a font, Ctrl+click to pick several. To

h: Choosing the fonts that stand in Turning the dialog box off and on Other ways to deal with missing fonts
x: Missing fonts A drawing made on another computer can use fonts that are not installed on yours. TraceDraw always shows such text in an installed font that looks close, and keeps the text's own font name. When the drawing opens, the Missing Fonts dialog box lets you choose which installed font draws each missing one, for now or for good. Choosing the fonts that stand in When you open a drawing with missing fonts, the Missing Fonts dialog box lists them: Each row shows the Missing font and the font it is Drawn with now. The first choice in the list is the font TraceDraw picked by itself, marked "(automatic)": a font drawn to the same widths when there is one, else one of the same style. To use another font, open the list of the row and click an installed family. Type part of a name in Find a font to narrow the lists. Choose how long the choice holds: For this session only (the drawing keeps its fonts) (the default): the font you chose draws the text until TraceDraw closes, bold and italic text included. The drawing keeps its own font names, so it is saved with them and shows in its own fonts on a computer that has them. Replace in the drawing (saved with it): every text in the missing family, also in groups, clip frames, tables and symbols, takes the font you chose. This changes the drawing and undoes in one step. Click OK. Cancel, Esc or the close button change nothing: the automatic fonts stay. Either way, the status bar then names the fonts still missing and the fonts that draw them, or says they were replaced. When some objects of the file could not be read, their note follows the dialog box. Turning the dialog box off and on Tick Do not show this message again in the dialog box to stop it. The drawing then opens straight away and the status bar names the missing fonts. Click that note on the status bar to open the Warnings page of Tools > Options > Global, where Ask which installed font draws each missing one (the Missing Fonts dialog) turns the dialog box on again (it is on at first). When an opened drawing uses fonts that are not installed, on the same page, is a separate, plain message that only names the missing fonts after the drawing opens. Opening drawings from scripts, the command line or the AI connection never stops at this dialog box. Other ways to deal with missing fonts Install the fonts, or add their folder in the Font Manager (see Fonts and glyphs); the text then shows in them. In the Fonts panel, families the drawing uses that are not installed are marked missing. Drawings saved as .tdraw and .cdr files with Embed fonts carry their fonts along, and a package holds the font files in its Fonts folder. The preflight lists text in fonts that are not installed before you print or publish.

h: The Writing Tools dialog box Spell Checker Dictionaries Grammar Thesaurus Autocorrect Custom hyphens Change case Text statistics Encode Web-compatible text
x: Writing tools TraceDraw checks spelling and grammar, finds synonyms, corrects as you type, and fixes text that came in with the wrong characters. The commands are in Text > Writing Tools and the Text menu. The Writing Tools dialog box Text > Writing Tools > Spell Check, Grammar and Thesaurus open the Writing Tools dialog box at that tab. Check chooses whether to check every text of the page (Document) or only the selected texts (Selection).  Spell Checker Click Start. The first word not found shows, with suggestions under Replacements. Click a suggestion to put it in Replace with (double-click to replace at once), or type the right word. Click Replace for this place, Auto Replace for every place, Skip Once or Skip All to leave it, or Add to add the word to your own word list. Undo takes back the last replacement. Options has Ignore words with numbers, Ignore words in capitals and Add corrections to Autocorrect. Dictionaries TraceDraw checks spelling with Hunspell dictionaries: for each language a .dic file and an .aff file with the same name, such as pt_BR.dic and pt_BR.aff. Free dictionaries for most languages can be downloaded from the projects that make them; other programs often install them too. Open Tools > Options > Text > Spelling. Click Open Folder and copy the .dic and .aff files into that folder (folders inside it work too), or name a folder that already has dictionaries in Also read dictionaries from. Click Read Again. The Dictionaries list shows each one; clear a box to stop using it. A word is right when any dictionary in use knows it. Dictionaries installed on your system are used as well. Without any, only a built-in word list is used. Hyphenation dictionaries (hyph_ files such as hyph_pt_BR.dic) go in the same folders. Choose one under Text > Paragraph Text > Hyphenation patterns to hyphenate text in that language. Grammar The grammar checker finds doubled words, double spaces, spaces before punctuation, missing spaces after it, sentences that start in lower case, unbalanced brackets and quotes, repeated punctuation, sentences over 40 words, missing end marks and, in English, "a" and "an" before the wrong sound. For each finding it shows the replacement, the New sentence and the Rule Name. Click Start (then Replace), Skip Once or Skip Rule. Thesaurus Type a word (the first word of the selected text at first) and click Look Up. The meanings show with their synonyms: click one to pick it, double-click to look it up. Insert puts it in the text, keeping the capitals. Under Options, Close after inserting closes the dialog box after inserting, and Choose Thesaurus File uses a thesaurus file you have. Autocorrect Text > Writing Tools > Autocorrect opens the Autocorrect tab of Tools > Options > Text, which sets what is corrected while you type: Capitalize first letter of sentences; Correct two initial capitals ("THe" becomes "The"); Capitalize names of days ("monday" becomes "Monday"); Automatically create hyperlinks when typing web addresses: typing www.example.com or an address starting with http:// or https:// gives the text object that hyperlink, unless it has one; Language the language whose quotation marks are used (the interface language unless you pick another); Use typographic quotation marks, and Use straight quotation marks after numbers (e.g. 6'); Single quotes and Double quotes: the Open and Close marks, if you want others than the language's; the Replacement table, used when Replace text while typing is on: (c) becomes ©, (r) ®, (tm) ™, 1/2 ½ and so on. Type in Replace and With, then click Add; click a row to Delete it, or change its text and click Replace. Apply to Selection applies the rules to the selected text. Text you paste or import is never changed.  Custom hyphens Text > Custom Optional Hyphens (also the gear of the Paragraph section of the Text panel) defines where your own words may break, such as product names. Those words break only there when hyphenation is on. Choose the Language (Show all languages lists every one). Type the Word and the Hyphenated Word with hyphens where it may break, such as Trace-Draw. Click Add Definition. Remove Definition removes the selected definition. Under Automatically insert custom optional hyphens, When typing and When pasting and importing text turn hyphenation on for texts that hold a defined word. Click Apply to Selection to apply them to the selected text now, or OK to keep them.  Change case Text > Change Case (Shift+F3) changes the selected text to Sentence case, lowercase, UPPERCASE, Title Case or tOGGLE cASE.  Text statistics Text > Text Statistics counts the text objects, lines, words, characters and fonts of the selected text, or of the page.  Encode Text that came from another program sometimes shows the wrong characters, such as "cafÃ©" instead of "café". Text > Encode fixes it: Select the text. Choose how the text Text was read as and what It really is (UTF-8, Windows-1252, ISO-8859-1, Mac OS Roman or Windows-1251). Check the Preview and click OK.  Web-compatible text Text > Make Text Web-compatible simplifies the selected text for web pages: gradient, pattern, texture and mesh fills become a flat color, and outlines, shadows and effects are removed.

Vorlagen und Stile Vorlagen und Stile sparen Arbeit, die Sie sonst wiederholen würden. Eine Vorlage ist eine fertige Zeichnung als Ausgangspunkt. Ein Stil ist ein benannter Satz aus Füllung, Umriss und Transparenz, der mit den Objekten verbunden bleibt, die ihn nutzen, sodass eine Änderung sie alle umgestaltet. Die Standardeigenschaften bestimmen, wie neue Objekte aussehen. Farbstile, die für einzelne Farben genauso funktionieren, erklärt Farbstile.

h: Mit einer Vorlage beginnen Die integrierten Vorlagen Eigene Vorlagen speichern
x: Vorlagen Eine Vorlage ist eine Zeichnung, mit der Sie beginnen: eine leere Seite in einer gängigen Größe oder eine gestaltete Visitenkarte, ein Flyer, ein Poster, ein Briefkopf oder ein Etikett zum Ausfüllen. Das Öffnen einer Vorlage erstellt eine neue, unbenannte Zeichnung; die Vorlage selbst ändert sich nie. Mit einer Vorlage beginnen Wählen Sie Datei > Neu aus Vorlage oder klicken Sie auf dem Begrüßungsbildschirm auf Neu aus Vorlage. Suchen Sie eine Vorlage: Geben Sie in Vorlagen suchen etwas ein, um Namen und Kategorien zu durchsuchen; wählen Sie die Herkunft der Vorlagen: Alle Vorlagen, Mitgeliefert oder Meine Vorlagen; wählen Sie eine Kategorie oder Alle Kategorien. Klicken Sie auf eine Vorlage, um sie anzusehen. Ist Vorlagendetails anzeigen eingeschaltet, zeigt der Bereich rechts sie groß mit Kategorie, Seitengröße und Quelle. Klicken Sie auf Öffnen, doppelklicken Sie auf die Vorlage oder drücken Sie Enter. Der Regler Größe unten macht die Miniaturen größer oder kleiner, und Vorlage öffnen öffnet jede .tdt- oder .tdraw-Datei als Vorlage.  Die integrierten Vorlagen Leere Seiten: A4 Hoch- und Querformat, A3, Letter, Visitenkarte (90 mal 50 mm), A2-Poster, Web (1920 mal 1080 Pixel) und Social Media (1080 mal 1080 Pixel). Gestaltet: zwei Visitenkarten, ein Angebotsflyer und ein Veranstaltungsflyer, ein Poster, ein Briefkopf, eine Urkunde, eine Rechnung, ein Geburtstagsbanner, ein Zitatbeitrag und ein rundes Etikett. Sie bestehen aus gewöhnlichen Formen und Text mit Beispieltext, sodass Sie jeden Teil ändern können. Eigene Vorlagen speichern Erstellen Sie die Zeichnung, mit der Sie künftig beginnen möchten. Wählen Sie Datei > Als Vorlage speichern. Geben Sie ihr einen Namen und speichern Sie sie. Gespeicherte Vorlagen erscheinen unter Meine Vorlagen. Sie liegen im Vorlagenordner Ihrer Einstellungen und sind daher in der Browserversion nicht verfügbar.

h: Default properties Changing defaults with nothing selected Styles To make a style Using and changing styles
x: Object styles and default properties The Object Styles panel has two parts: the Default Properties of new objects, and the styles of the drawing. Both are saved with the drawing. Open it from Window > Panels, or right-click an object and choose the object styles panel.  Default properties New objects take the fill and outline of their kind: Graphic: shapes, lines, tables and everything except text no fill, a thin black outline Artistic text: text without a frame black fill, no outline Paragraph text: text in a frame black fill, no outline In the panel, each kind shows its fill and outline, with From Selection (take the fill and outline of the selected object) and Reset (back to the defaults of a new drawing). Changing defaults with nothing selected When nothing is selected and you choose a fill or outline (click a palette color, use a fill tool, change the outline color or width), the change goes to new objects. TraceDraw asks which kinds of new objects it applies to: Tick Graphic, Artistic text and Paragraph text as needed. The kinds you ticked last time are ticked. Tick Use these kinds from now on without asking to skip the question from now on. Click OK. Cancel changes nothing.  The check box Ask which kinds a change with nothing selected applies to in the panel turns the question on or off. The Properties panel with nothing selected also edits the Graphic defaults. To keep the defaults for every new drawing, choose Tools > Save Settings as Default. Styles A style is a named set of properties: Fill, Outline (its color, width, line style and arrowheads) and Transparency. Objects you give a style stay linked to it: change the style and they all change. To make a style Select an object with the look you want. Click New style from selection. The style is named "Style 1" and so on, takes the fill, outline and transparency of the object, and is linked to every selected object. Using and changing styles Each style shows its swatches, its name (click it to rename), how many objects are linked to it, and its parts as check boxes: Apply gives the selection the style and links it. Update from selection takes the fill, outline and transparency of the selected object; every linked object follows. Turning a part off leaves that property to each object. Delete removes the style; linked objects keep their look. Break Link to Style unlinks the selected objects, which keep their look. You can still change a linked object directly; the next change of its style sets the style's parts again. Right-click an object to apply a style from its menu.

Seiten und Layout Eine Zeichnung kann viele Seiten haben, jede mit eigener Größe und Ausrichtung. Diese Seiten erklären, wie Sie Seiten hinzufügen, anordnen und nummerieren, die Dokumentoptionen einstellen (Seitengröße, Layout, Hintergrund, Anschnitt, Lineale, Raster und Hilfslinien), Hilfslinien setzen, Objekte einrasten lassen und die Eigenschaften einer Zeichnung lesen.

h: Moving between pages The Pages panel Inserting pages Deleting pages Duplicating a page Renaming a page Page size and orientation Page numbers Page background
x: Working with pages Moving between pages Click a page tab under the drawing window, or use the page navigator beside them (first, previous, next and last page). Press PgUp or PgDn. Choose Layout > Go to Page, type the page number in the Go To Page dialog box and click OK.  The Pages panel The Pages panel lists the pages of the drawing. Click a page to go to it. Its buttons Insert Page, Delete Page and Duplicate Page act on the current page, and Page Sorter View shows every page as a thumbnail. Open it from Window > Panels.  Inserting pages Choose Layout > Insert Page, or click one of the insert buttons of the page navigator (they add one page of the current size before or after the current page at once). In the Insert Page dialog box, set the Number of pages and choose Before or After the current page. Click OK.  Deleting pages Delete Page asks which pages to delete: the page number in Delete page (the current page to start with), and to delete a range, Through to page with the last page of it. All of them go in one step, which Undo brings back. A drawing keeps at least one page. Delete Page on a page tab's menu deletes that page at once. Duplicating a page Choose Layout > Duplicate Page, or right-click the page tab and choose Duplicate Page. Under Insert new page, choose Before selected page or After selected page. Choose Copy layer(s) only for a page with the same layers and nothing on them, or Copy layer(s) and their contents to copy the objects too. Click OK. The copy becomes the current page; Edit > Undo removes it. The page tab menu also has Insert Page After, Insert Page Before, Delete Page and Switch Page Orientation. Renaming a page Choose Layout > Rename Page, or double-click the page tab. Type the Page name and click OK.  Page size and orientation Layout > Page Size opens the Page Size dialog box: Type the Width and Height; Swap exchanges them. Tick Apply to all pages to change every page, or leave it off to change the current page only. Click OK.  Switch Page Orientation turns the page between portrait and landscape. With nothing selected, the property bar of the Pick tool also sets the page size and orientation. Its page size list has A4, Letter, A5, A3 and Legal first, then the sizes you saved, then about 130 sizes in groups (ISO A, ISO B and JIS B, North American, print shop, posters and banners, envelopes, cards and postcards, photo, screen and social media, web ads). Custom... opens the Page Size dialog box, and Edit This List... opens the document options at the page size, where you can save a size under a name. The full page settings are in Document options. Pages you add, and their first layer, are named in the interface language. Page numbers Layout > Insert Page Number puts a page number On Active Layer, On All Pages, On All Odd Pages or On All Even Pages. The numbers on master layers show the right number on every page. Object > Insert > Page Number places one in the text you are editing. Layout > Page Number Settings sets how they look: Start at: the first number; Prefix and Suffix: text around the number, such as "Page "; Style: 1, 2, 3, I, II, III, i, ii, iii, A, B, C or a, b, c; Position: Bottom centre, Bottom outer corner, Top centre or Top outer corner.  Page background Layout > Page Background sets the color behind every page; see Document options.

h: Die Anordnung In der Mehrseitenansicht arbeiten
x: Mehrseitenansicht Maschinelle Übersetzung: Diese Seite kann hinter der englischen Fassung zurückliegen. Ansicht > Multipage View legt alle Seiten der Zeichnung gleichzeitig auf dem Desktop aus, sodass Sie Seiten vergleichen und nebeneinander bearbeiten können. Die Anordnung Die Seiten liegen in Seitenreihenfolge in einem Raster aus vier Spalten; eine neue Seite kommt an den nächsten Platz, und die Seiten davor bleiben, wo sie waren. Unter jeder Seite stehen ihre Nummer und ihr Name; die der aktuellen Seite in der normalen Textfarbe, die anderen abgeblendet. In der Mehrseitenansicht arbeiten Die aktuelle Seite wird wie gewohnt bearbeitet: Lineale, Hilfslinien, Gitter und die Statusleiste beziehen sich auf sie. Klicken oder ziehen Sie auf einer anderen Seite, um sie zur aktuellen zu machen und sofort dort zu arbeiten. Auch die Seitenregister und der Navigator wechseln die aktuelle Seite. Auf Fenstergröße zoomen (F4) passt alle Seiten ins Fenster ein. Die Schaltfläche mit vier kleinen Seiten in der Seitenleiste, gleich nach den Seitensteuerelementen, schaltet die Ansicht ebenfalls ein und aus; sie leuchtet, solange die Ansicht an ist. Wählen Sie erneut Multipage View, um wieder zu einer Seite auf einmal zurückzukehren. Seitensortierungsansicht zeigt die Seiten stattdessen als Miniaturen; die beiden Ansichten schließen einander aus.

h: General Page size Layout Background Bleed Rulers Grid Guidelines
x: Document options Layout > Document Options opens the settings of the active drawing: page size, layout, background, bleed, rulers, grid and guidelines. Double-clicking a ruler or the page border also opens it. Choose a page from the list on the left. Changes show at once; OK keeps them and Cancel puts everything back. Save as default keeps the grid, ruler and guideline settings for new drawings. General  Rendering resolution: the resolution of effects that are turned into pixels, such as drop shadows and bitmap effects. Fill open curves (off at first): when on, open curves show their fill as if they were closed. Auto inflate bitmaps for effects (on at first): bitmaps grow to make room for effects that spread past their edges. Duplicate offset: how far Duplicate places the copy. Page size  Choose Page size for a paper size, or Label presets for sheets of labels, which set the page to the sheet size and add guidelines around each label. Size, Width and Height, and Portrait or Landscape. The save button next to Size keeps a custom size under a name you type, and the delete button forgets the saved size shown. Saved sizes appear in every page size list: the property bar, the Page Size dialog box, these options and the new document dialog box. Apply size to current page only: change the current page only. Show page border, and Add Page Frame, which adds a rectangle the size of the page. Rendering resolution, Bleed and Show bleed area (see below). Layout  The page shows how many pages the drawing has, with Page Sorter View and Switch Page Orientation, and lists the Master layers, each shown on All pages, Odd pages or Even pages. The buttons add a new master layer for all, odd or even pages. See Master layers. Background  Choose No background, a Solid color, or a Bitmap (Choose bitmap) to show behind every page. Bleed  Bleed is the part of the drawing that runs past the edge of the page, so the print has no white edge once trimmed. Set the Bleed distance and tick Show bleed area to see it. Printing and PDF export can include the bleed; see Printing. Rulers  Units: the drawing units (inches, millimeters, picas, points, pixels, ciceros, didots, feet, yards, miles, centimeters, meters or kilometers). Drawing scale: makes a distance on the page stand for a distance in the world, such as 1:100. Choose a typical scale, or type the page distance and the world distance. Rulers, positions, sizes and new dimension lines then show world distances; page sizes, outline widths and text sizes do not. Origin: where the rulers count from (Horizontal and Vertical); Reset origin to the page corner puts it back. You can also drag the origin out of the corner where the rulers meet. Tick divisions: the number of ticks between ruler numbers. Nudge: the Nudge distance of the arrow keys (2.54 mm), the Super nudge with Shift (5.08 mm) and the Micro nudge with Ctrl (0.254 mm). Show rulers. Grid  Document grid: Show grid, Snap to grid, the Horizontal and Vertical spacing (10 mm at first), as a distance or as lines per unit, and Show grid as Lines or Dots. Baseline grid: lines across the page for lining up text, with the Baseline grid spacing (14 points), the Start from top (12.7 mm) and the Line color. Pixel grid: the Color and Opacity of the grid of pixels, Show grid at 800% or higher zoom and Snap to pixels. Guidelines  Show guidelines and Snap to guidelines. Default guideline color and Default preset guideline color. Presets: one inch margins, bleed area, page borders, printable area, a three-column newsletter, a basic grid and an upper left grid. User defined: Margins (Top, Bottom, Left, Right), Columns (Number of columns and Distance between) and a Grid (Rows and Columns). Apply Presets adds them; a line that is already there is not added twice. See Rulers, grids and guidelines for working with guidelines on the page.

h: Rulers The document grid Guidelines The Guidelines panel
x: Rulers, grids and guidelines Rulers, grids and guidelines help you place objects precisely. None of them print. Rulers The rulers run along the top and left of the drawing window, in the drawing units; View > Rulers shows or hides them. A dashed line on each ruler follows the pointer. Drag from the corner where the rulers meet to move the origin, the point the rulers count from. Positions on the property bar, the status bar and in the panels count from it too. Drag from a ruler to add a guideline. Double-click a ruler to open its settings; see Document options, where you also set the units and the drawing scale. The document grid View > Grid > Document Grid shows a grid of lines or dots over the page, behind the objects; Document Grid in Snap To makes objects snap to it. Its spacing (10 mm at first) is set in Document options. When lines would be too close, only every second, fifth or tenth line is drawn. The baseline grid (Baseline Grid) draws lines across the page like a ruled notebook, for lining up text; the pixel grid (Pixel Grid) shows the pixels of the drawing in the Pixels view from 800% zoom. Guidelines Guidelines are lines across the drawing window that objects can snap to. Drag from the top ruler for a horizontal guideline, from the left ruler for a vertical one. With the Pick tool, click a guideline to select it (Shift+click adds), and drag it to move it. Drop it outside the drawing window, or press Delete, to delete it. Click the selected guideline again to show its rotation handles, and drag them to turn it. Right-click a guideline to delete, lock or unlock it, or open its properties. Locked guidelines can be selected but not moved or deleted. Edit > Select All > Guidelines selects every guideline of the page, and Guidelines shows or hides them. With guidelines selected (and no objects), Copy and Paste make copies in the same place, and Duplicate makes copies moved by the duplicate offset (set in Layout > Document Options, General). The Transformations panel moves, rotates and scales selected guidelines as it does objects. The Guidelines panel The Guidelines panel places guidelines by their coordinates. Open it from Window > Panels.  Show and Snap turn guidelines on and snapping to them. Choose the Guideline type: horizontal, vertical or angled. Type the position (x, y, and the Angle for an angled one), counted from the ruler origin. Click Add to add a guideline, or select one in the list and click Modify to move it. The list shows the page's guidelines of that type (Ctrl+click to select several). Delete, Lock and Unlock act on the selected ones, and Guideline color and Guideline style (Solid, Dashed, Dotted or Dash dot) change their look. Ready-made sets of guidelines (margins, columns, grids) are on the Guidelines page of the document options.

h: Turning snapping on and off What objects snap to Snapping while moving Dynamic and alignment guides
x: Snapping Snapping pulls the pointer, and the objects you move, onto exact points: nodes, the middles of segments, the centers of shapes, guidelines, the grid or the page. It makes it easy to join lines and line objects up without zooming in. Turning snapping on and off View > Snap To, or the Snap To list on the standard toolbar, turns snapping to Pixels, Document Grid (Ctrl+Y), Baseline Grid, Guidelines, Objects (Alt+Z) and Page on and off. At first objects, guidelines and the page are on. The baseline grid works on its own too: with only it on, nodes and objects snap to its lines. Snap Off (Alt+Q) turns all snapping off and on again. What objects snap to When snapping to objects is on, these points attract the pointer within the snapping radius (10 screen pixels at first). Each shows its mark and, with screen tips on, its name. Node the nodes of outlines, the corners of rectangles, the points of polygons Intersection where two outlines cross Midpoint halfway along each segment Quadrant the top, bottom, left and right of ellipses Tangent where a line you draw touches an ellipse or curve Perpendicular where a line you draw meets a segment at a right angle Edge the nearest point of an outline Center the center of shapes, bitmaps and tables Text baseline the baseline of a line of text Points win over guidelines, guidelines over the grids, and edges come last. The modes, the radius and the marks are set on the Snapping page of the options; see TraceDraw options. Snapping while moving When you start moving a selection with the Pick tool on one of its points (a node, a midpoint or the center), that point is carried onto the other object's point or edge. Otherwise the edges and center of the selection's box snap to guidelines, grids, the page and other objects. The handles snap while you resize. Dynamic and alignment guides View > Dynamic Guides (Alt+Shift+D) shows temporary guides at 0, 45, 90 and 135 degrees through the points you pass over, so you can draw along them. Alignment Guides (Alt+Shift+A) shows guides when the object you move lines up with others.

h: Describing the drawing The report
x: Document properties File > Document Properties opens the Document Properties dialog box. It keeps information about the drawing, such as its title and author, and reports everything the drawing holds.  Describing the drawing Language: the language of the drawing's text, or none. PDF files written from the drawing carry it, which helps screen readers. Title, Subject, Author, Copyright, Tags (keywords written to PDF and SVG files) and Notes (several lines). Rating: none or one to five stars. Click OK to keep the changes, as one undo step. Cancel leaves everything as it was. The title, subject and rating can also be set when you save; see Save As. The report Under the fields, a report lists what the drawing holds, in sections: File: the name and location of the file. Document: the pages and layers, the page size (in the drawing units and in pixels), the orientation and the resolution. Color: the color profiles, the primary color mode and the rendering intent. Graphic Objects: the number of objects and of points, the most points and parts one curve has, and the curves, rectangles, ellipses, polygons, groups and tables. Text Statistics: artistic and paragraph texts, characters, words and the fonts used. Bitmap Objects: the number of bitmaps, their total pixels and the largest one. Styles: object and color styles. Effects: each effect, with how many objects use it. Fills and Outlines: the objects by kind of fill and outline, and how many use each color model. Symbols: symbols defined and instances placed. The report helps before sending a file to print: for example, it shows which fonts the drawing needs and whether it holds RGB colors. For a full check, see Preflight.

Bitmaps Bitmaps sind Bilder aus Pixeln, etwa Fotos und Scans. TraceDraw platziert sie in Zeichnungen, ändert ihren Farbmodus und ihre Größe, richtet sie gerade, maskiert Farben, wendet Effekte an und vektorisiert sie zu Formen. Es wandelt auch Vektorobjekte in Bitmaps um. Um ein Bild hereinzuholen, verwenden Sie Datei > Importieren; siehe Dateien importieren. Ist ein Bitmap ausgewählt, enthält die Eigenschaftsleiste die Bitmap-Befehle: bearbeiten, zuschneiden, vektorisieren, gerade richten und neu berechnen. Zu Effekten siehe Bitmap-Effekte.

h: Einstellungen
x: Objekte in Bitmaps umwandeln Bitmaps > In Bitmap konvertieren (auch Objekt > In Bitmap konvertieren) wandelt die ausgewählten Objekte in eine einzige Bitmap um. Damit können Sie komplexe Grafiken reduzieren oder Objekte für Bitmap-Effekte vorbereiten. Es ist ein einziger Rückgängig-Schritt.  Einstellungen Auflösung: Wählen Sie aus der Liste (72 bis 600 dpi) oder geben Sie einen Wert ein (36 bis 2400; anfangs 300). Farbmodus: Schwarzweiß (1 Bit), Graustufen (8 Bit), Palette (8 Bit), RGB-Farbe (24 Bit, anfangs) oder CMYK-Farbe (32 Bit). Gerastert: Bei Schwarzweiß und Palette werden Punkte gemischt, um die fehlenden Farbtöne anzudeuten. Schwarz immer überdrucken: Das Schwarz der Bitmap wird über die darunter liegenden Farben gedruckt. Kantenglättung (anfangs ein): glatte Kanten; aus ergibt harte Pixelkanten. Transparenter Hintergrund (anfangs ein); aus legt die Objekte auf Weiß. Das Dialogfeld zeigt, wie groß die Bitmap unkomprimiert wird.

t: Changing the color mode of bitmaps
h: Black and white Duotone Paletted Coloring black and white bitmaps
x: Changing the color mode of bitmaps Bitmaps > Mode converts the selected bitmaps to another color mode. Every selected bitmap changes in one undo step, and transparency is kept. The modes with settings open a dialog box you can size, with the picture before and after the change in the Before and After preview on the left and the settings on the right. Black and White (1-bit) black and white only (see below) Grayscale (8-bit) shades of gray Duotone (8-bit) one to four inks (see below) Paletted (8-bit) at most 256 colors (see below) RGB Color (24-bit) the bitmap's mode becomes RGB; the pixels stay as they are Lab Color (24-bit) Lab color CMYK Color (32-bit) the bitmap's mode becomes CMYK and its pixels show the colors the inks can print, worked out with the color management profiles The menu ticks RGB Color (24-bit) or CMYK Color (32-bit) when every selected bitmap is in that mode, and the status bar names the mode of a selected bitmap, such as "Bitmap 600 x 400 px (CMYK)". A CMYK picture of a .cdr file opens in the CMYK mode, and .tdraw files keep the mode. Tools > Convert Colors sets the mode of every bitmap it converts in the same way (see Converting colors). Black and white  Choose the conversion method: Line art: white where the gray is at or above the threshold (128 at first), black elsewhere; Ordered: a regular pattern of dots; Halftone (at first): a screen of round, line or square dots at an angle (45 degrees) and a number of lines per inch (60); Cardinality-distribution: a random-looking texture; Jarvis, Stucki and Floyd-Steinberg: error diffusion, the smoothest results for photos. Intensity (0 to 100, 50 at first) makes the result lighter or darker. Duotone  A duotone prints a grayscale picture with a few inks, which gives rich tones with few colors. Choose the type: Monotone, Duotone (at first), Tritone or Quadtone, for one to four inks. Click an ink to change its color. Edit its curve: across is the gray level (black on the left), up is how much of that ink prints. Drag on empty space to add a point, drag a point to move it, double-click it or drag it off the grid to remove it. Show all draws the other inks' curves too.
